words.gram: colloquial variant of すみません

lines.trans: It's me! Long time no see, Mr. Kawada.
He's working at my store right now—said he had nowhere else to go.
Now for the main reason I called you two here: our store chain is talking about releasing our own original adult videos.
Videos don't sell like they used to, and the wholesalers are taking advantage of us.

words.gram: Auxiliary na-adjective expressing appearance or likeness.

lines.trans: So we figured, why not produce and sell them ourselves? We can even put up a bit of funding.
Let's do it.
All right, it's a deal—make us something incredible!

words.gram: Plain imperative of くれる (give/do for me).

lines.trans: We'll simply make what we want to make. Let us show you what lies beyond the mosaic.
What lies beyond the mosaic—I look forward to seeing it!

words.gloss: something to look forward to; fun

lines.trans: Come on, whip off that apron—you go with them too!
I'll gladly join you! Yes!
Excuse me, I'll take all of these.

meanings.note: Very common colloquial pronunciation/variant of すみません.

examples.text: すいません、ちょっと通してください。
examples.trans: Excuse me, please let me through.

meanings.note: Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.
With で (全部で), means 'in total' or 'altogether'.
Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: First-person pronoun commonly used by men and boys in friendly or polite everyday settings.

examples.text: 僕もコーヒーをください。

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Meaning: Mitamura.

examples.text: 三田村ちゃんと豚足食え

meanings.note: Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.
Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 彼女は来るんだろうな？
ちゃんとキャストはそろってるんだろうな？
examples.trans: You've got the whole cast properly lined up, right?

meanings.note: Can stand at the head of a sentence without a particle ('right now').
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Native counter reading ふたり; shops politely say お二人様 for 'party of two'.

examples.trans: The two of us go together.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.

examples.text: 二人を呼んだ本題だ。今うちのチェーンでオリジナルのアダルトビデオを出そうっていう話になってる。
examples.trans: Now for the main reason I called you two here: our store chain is talking about releasing our own original adult videos.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

examples.text: 二人を呼んだ本題だ。今うちのチェーンでオリジナルのアダルトビデオを出そうっていう話になってる。
examples.trans: Now for the main reason I called you two here: our store chain is talking about releasing our own original adult videos.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 二人を呼んだ本題だ。今うちのチェーンでオリジナルのアダルトビデオを出そうっていう話になってる。
examples.trans: Now for the main reason I called you two here: our store chain is talking about releasing our own original adult videos.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

meanings.note: Covers everything from a casual chat to a business deal or idea.

examples.trans: Let us have a little talk.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

meanings.note: Auxiliary na-adjective expressing resemblance or conjecture.

examples.trans: It looks like it's going to rain.

examples.text: 彼は忙しいみたいですね。

meanings.note: Intransitive verb describing goods selling on the market without naming a seller.

examples.text: この絵本はよく売れます。
新しい本がたくさん売れました。
examples.trans: Many copies of the new book sold.

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Between の and な (あなたのような人), describes someone or something 'like ...'.

examples.text: 春のような暖かい日です。
examples.trans: It is a warm day like spring.

examples.text: あなたのような人を探していました。
examples.trans: I was looking for someone like you.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Attaches to the irrealis (a-stem) of godan verbs.

examples.trans: I was called by the teacher.

meanings.note: Colloquial conjunction built from だ + たら.
て-form 売って links 'sell' into the next action.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Calls someone's attention ('look here!') or asks for a brief pause (ちょっと待って).

examples.text: ちょっと待ってください。
ちょっと見てください。

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.en: open a store; bring out; hand in
meanings.note: 店を出す means opening a branch; 出しやがって attaches tough-guy disdainful やがる.

examples.text: 駅前に新しい店を出します。
examples.trans: We open a new branch in front of the station.

examples.text: 書類を出してください。

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Satisfied exclamation when gearing up or finishing a task cleanly.

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。
今日は皆様にモザイクの向こう側をお見せいたします。
examples.trans: Today I will show all of you the world beyond censorship.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.

examples.trans: All of our satellite lines are already full.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 脱いでもらう前に、まず君の心を裸にしたい。
examples.trans: Before you take off your clothes, first I want to bare your heart.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Blunt or rowdy second-person pronoun used with subordinates, rivals, or close crew.

examples.trans: I leave it to you guys.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Everyday reading あした; pairs with また in また明日 ('see you tomorrow').
